sources.title: Tokio spawn_blocking
sources.locator: Function description and cancellation/runtime shutdown, lines 31–38
sources.observed_operation: A large configurable blocking-thread ceiling is used; started spawn_blocking closures cannot be aborted, and shutdown can wait indefinitely unless shutdown_timeout stops waiting.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The API is intended for blocking work that eventually finishes; shutdown_timeout does not cancel a started closure.
sources.applicability: Tokio Rust code using spawn_blocking; supports avoiding it as the only containment boundary for untrusted or stuck parsing.

sources.title: Windows Job Objects
sources.version_or_commit: Current Microsoft Win32 documentation; page accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: Managing Processes in Jobs, Job Limits, Managing a Process Tree that Uses Job Objects
sources.observed_operation: CreateProcess children join the job by default; breakaway flags can change that; a job can terminate associated processes and enforce limits; nested jobs begin with Windows 8 / Server 2012.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Other process-creation paths and breakaway settings can escape; pre-Windows 8 nesting behavior differs.
sources.applicability: Windows renderer supervision and resource controls; Job Objects do not provide filesystem or network sandboxing.

sources.title: Landlock: unprivileged access control
sources.version_or_commit: Linux kernel documentation dated August 2026; ABI and rights depend on running kernel
sources.locator: Defining/enforcing a policy and ABI compatibility, lines 62–106, 176–228; network rights lines 23–26; descriptor semantics lines 270–282
sources.observed_operation: Unprivileged enforcement requires no_new_privs; applications query ABI and mask unsupported rights. TCP network rules begin at ABI 4 and UDP at ABI 10. Some rights are bound to opened file descriptors; preconnected datagram sockets are not constrained by later IPC scoping.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Only operations covered by handled rights are denied by default; old ABIs lack later network controls; already-open descriptors and sockets require deliberate handling.
sources.applicability: Optional Linux filesystem/network sandbox backend only when runtime ABI, rights, descriptor state, and policy are sufficient.

sources.title: Thumbnail Managing Standard
sources.locator: Thumb::MTime / Thumb::Size metadata and Detect Modifications, lines 180–185 and 261–278
sources.observed_operation: The standard stores mtime in seconds and recommends checking size; it warns that multiple files can share the one-second mtime and that mtime alone can leave an incorrect thumbnail.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: This is a cache interoperability/freshness standard, not a generic thumbnail-service API; size is an additional check, not proof of identical content.
sources.applicability: Linux/XDG thumbnail cache precedent; does not substantiate the draft's generic Linux user thumbnail service alternative.

sources.title: Zotero attachmentPreview.js
sources.observed_operation: Latest-task bookkeeping is processed in order on the normal path; each render races against a 3-second delay, after which flags are reset regardless. A losing render promise is not cancelled by Promise.race. Item-ID equality is checked before and after awaited render work.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A UI component/renderer precedent in Zotero 7.0.12, not an OS process boundary. The 3-second timeout frees bookkeeping, not necessarily the underlying render.
sources.applicability: Supports latest-task coalescing and an item-ID acceptance check; does not support an unconditional claim that timed-out work is serialized or terminated.

sources.title: XPC — Apple Developer Documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current Apple Developer Documentation as retrieved 2026-10-12; no release version or commit listed
sources.locator: Overview and XPC Service process-environment table
sources.observed_operation: launchd starts bundled XPC services on demand, shuts them down when idle, and restarts them after crashes; the page describes request/reply connections and privilege isolation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The overview does not specify a per-request hard-cancel or bounded forced-stop contract for a hung handler; connection lifecycle should not be assumed to equal worker termination.
sources.applicability: Primary source for macOS XPC service lifecycle; the proposal must separately establish its timeout, kill/restart, and shutdown behavior.
